text: Why is analog photonic linear algebra 'condition-number sensitive' in a way that floating-point arithmetic is not?
choices: Because a high condition number requires more than N(N-1)/2 MZIs
Because the thermo-optic coefficient itself scales with the condition number
Because normalizing singular values by sigma_max attenuates the weak channels until shot noise dominates them, so ill-conditioned matrices lose ENOB on those channels
Because floating point also loses precision linearly with the condition number
explanation: After normalizing by sigma_max, channel i keeps only (sigma_i/sigma_max)^2 of the power, so for kappa >> 1 the weak singular channels are starved of photons, shot noise dominates, and their effective bits collapse. This is a photon-budget effect unique to analog optics; the MZI count stays fixed at N(N-1)/2 and the thermo-optic coefficient is independent of kappa.
